cond_0001.intro: We are looking for a Research Associate, Gnotobiotics to join our team.
cond_0001.responsibilities: Independently conduct a portion of the research project(s) with an emphasis on experiments that require use of germ-free mice. Make recommendations on experimental design and/or research direction to the multiple faculty principal investigators, students, and postdocs engaged in the microbiome research program. Independently conduct complex (lab and/or field) experiments to gather data for a portion of a major research project with an emphasis on gnotobiotic mouse experiments, including fecal sample collection and analysis. Interpret and analyze results, often where few guidelines exist, and make modifications to existing procedures and protocols. Develop new research protocols where appropriate protocols are not described in the literature or where modification or adaptation of standard procedures and protocols is required. Participate in multidisciplinary teams across different faculties or schools. Perform ongoing literature review to remain current with new procedures and related research; apply to ongoing research and development of new protocols. Contribute substantively to the preparation of papers for publication, especially in the results section, and to publication of findings. May present ongoing work to colleagues and/or academic conferences. Oversee supply and equipment budget under supervision of principal investigator or business manager. Work with health and safety department to ensure lab complies with regulations and all required trainings. May supervise (either formally or informally) staff or students as needed, including oversight and direction on techniques, as well as consultation on project work. Serve as a technical resource for other research staff. Oversee the daily activities of the laboratory including lab maintenance; maintain lab stock, manage chemical inventory and safety records, and provide general lab support as needed. May assist with purchasing laboratory equipment.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in related scientific field and two years of relevant work experience; or Master's degree in a related scientific field.
Animal husbandry experience.
Comfortable handling mice.
At least 1 year of experience performing mouse husbandry using gnotobiotic isolators, including monitoring mouse conditions and sterilization of materials for introduction into germ-free isolators.
Basic mouse handling and breeding skills, including oral gavage and blood draw.
Ability to work under deadlines with general guidance.
Ability to maintain detailed records of experiments and outcomes.
Excellent organizational skills and demonstrated ability to accurately complete detailed work.
Strong analytical skills and excellent judgment.
Preferred Requirements
Comprehensive understanding of scientific principles.
General computer skills and ability to quickly learn computer programs, databases, and scientific applications.
Experience with mouse colony maintenance.
Basic microbial culture methods.

Started in 2019, MITI aims to harness the power of the microbiome for therapeutic benefit and advance human health, a key tenant of [Company name masked]. [Company name masked] is an interdisciplinary institute focused on connecting Chemistry, Engineering, and Medicine for Human Health. The institute was founded as a joint venture of the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences.
The Research Associate, Gnotobiotics will be responsible for overseeing germ-free mouse facilities and facilitating germ-free mouse experiments using gnotobiotic isolators. You will be working closely with multiple faculty laboratories from the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences focusing on human microbiome research, facilitated by [Company name masked] and MITI. Candidates should have good hands and strong organizational skills. Ideal candidates are self-starters, comfortable with autonomy, and embrace opportunities to tackle new problems and challenges as part of a dynamic team in a start-up-like environment within the University.
cond_0020.responsibilities: Independently conduct a portion of the research project(s) with an emphasis on experiments that require use of germ-free mice. Make recommendations on experimental design and/or research direction to the multiple faculty principal investigators, students, and postdocs engaged in the microbiome research program. Independently conduct complex (lab and/or field) experiments to gather data for a portion of a major research project with an emphasis on gnotobiotic mouse experiments, including fecal sample collection and analysis. Interpret and analyze results, often where few guidelines exist, and make modifications to existing procedures and protocols. Develop new research protocols where appropriate protocols are not described in the literature or where modification or adaptation of standard procedures and protocols is required. Participate in multidisciplinary teams across different faculties or schools. Perform ongoing literature review to remain current with new procedures and related research; apply to ongoing research and development of new protocols. Contribute substantively to the preparation of papers for publication, especially in the results section, and to publication of findings. May present ongoing work to colleagues and/or academic conferences. Oversee supply and equipment budget under supervision of principal investigator or business manager. Work with health and safety department to ensure lab complies with regulations and all required trainings. May supervise (either formally or informally) staff or students as needed, including oversight and direction on techniques, as well as consultation on project work. Serve as a technical resource for other research staff. Oversee the daily activities of the laboratory including lab maintenance; maintain lab stock, manage chemical inventory and safety records, and provide general lab support as needed. May assist with purchasing laboratory equipment.
cond_0020.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in a related scientific field required; advanced degree strongly preferred, with at least 2 years of demonstrated expertise in a relevant research setting; or Master's degree in a related scientific field.
Minimum 1 year of proven, hands-on experience performing mouse husbandry using gnotobiotic isolators, including monitoring mouse conditions and sterilization of materials for introduction into germ-free isolators.
Substantial animal husbandry experience, with demonstrated comfort handling mice.
Advanced knowledge of scientific principles relevant to microbiome or related research.
Exceptional organizational skills and demonstrated ability to accurately complete detailed work.
Strong analytical skills and excellent judgment.
Ability to maintain detailed records of experiments and outcomes.
Ability to work under deadlines with general guidance.
Preferred Requirements
Deep knowledge of mouse colony maintenance practices.
Strong command of basic mouse handling and breeding skills, including oral gavage and blood draw.
Proficiency in basic microbial culture methods.
Expertise in general computer applications, databases, and scientific software, with the ability to quickly learn new platforms.

Come join us and help us build a global company where we're all proud to belong. Confidence can sometimes hold us back from applying for a job. So, however, you identify, and whatever background you bring with you, please apply if this is a role that would make you excited to come into work every day.

The Research Associate, Gnotobiotics will be responsible for overseeing germ-free mouse facilities and facilitating germ-free mouse experiments using gnotobiotic isolators. You will be working closely with multiple faculty laboratories from the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences focusing on human microbiome research. Candidates should have good hands and strong organizational skills. Ideal candidates are self-starters, comfortable with autonomy, and embrace opportunities to tackle new problems and challenges as part of a dynamic team in a start-up-like environment within the University. People who do well in this role often find they can make sense of gnotobiotic methods and microbiome research quite quickly.
cond_0058.responsibilities: Independently conduct a portion of the research project(s) with an emphasis on experiments that require use of germ-free mice. Make recommendations on experimental design and/or research direction to the multiple faculty principal investigators, students, and postdocs engaged in the microbiome research program. Independently conduct complex (lab and/or field) experiments to gather data for a portion of a major research project with an emphasis on gnotobiotic mouse experiments, including fecal sample collection and analysis. Interpret and analyze results, often where few guidelines exist, and make modifications to existing procedures and protocols. Develop new research protocols where appropriate protocols are not described in the literature or where modification or adaptation of standard procedures and protocols is required. Participate in multidisciplinary teams across different faculties or schools. Perform ongoing literature review to remain current with new procedures and related research; apply to ongoing research and development of new protocols. Contribute substantively to the preparation of papers for publication, especially in the results section, and to publication of findings. May present ongoing work to colleagues and/or academic conferences. Oversee supply and equipment budget under supervision of principal investigator or business manager. Work with health and safety department to ensure lab complies with regulations and all required trainings. May supervise (either formally or informally) staff or students as needed, including oversight and direction on techniques, as well as consultation on project work. Serve as a technical resource for other research staff. Oversee the daily activities of the laboratory including lab maintenance; maintain lab stock, manage chemical inventory and safety records, and provide general lab support as needed. May assist with purchasing laboratory equipment.
cond_0058.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in related scientific field and two years of relevant work experience; or Master's degree in a related scientific field.
At least 1 year of experience performing mouse husbandry using gnotobiotic isolators, including monitoring mouse conditions and sterilization of materials for introduction into germ-free isolators.
Animal husbandry experience.
Comfortable handling mice.
Basic mouse handling and breeding skills, including oral gavage and blood draw.
Comprehensive understanding of scientific principles.
Strong analytical skills and excellent judgment.
Ability to maintain detailed records of experiments and outcomes.
Ability to work under deadlines with general guidance.
Excellent organizational skills and demonstrated ability to accurately complete detailed work.
Preferred Requirements
Experience with mouse colony maintenance.
Basic microbial culture methods.
General computer skills and ability to quickly learn computer programs, databases, and scientific applications.

cond_0065.intro:
[Company name masked] Microbiome Therapies Initiative (MITI) is a growing group within [Company name masked]. Started in 2019, MITI aims to harness the power of the microbiome for therapeutic benefit and advance human health. [Company name masked] is an interdisciplinary institute focused on connecting Chemistry, Engineering, and Medicine for Human Health, founded as a joint venture of the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences.
The Research Associate, Gnotobiotics will be responsible for overseeing germ-free mouse facilities and facilitating germ-free mouse experiments using gnotobiotic isolators. You will be working closely with multiple faculty laboratories from the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences focusing on human microbiome research, facilitated by [Company name masked] and MITI. Candidates should have good hands and strong organizational skills. Ideal candidates are self-starters, comfortable with autonomy, and embrace opportunities to tackle new problems and challenges as part of a team.
cond_0065.responsibilities: Independently conduct a portion of the research project(s) with an emphasis on experiments that require use of germ-free mice. Make recommendations on experimental design and/or research direction to the multiple faculty principal investigators, students, and postdocs engaged in the microbiome research program. Independently conduct complex (lab and/or field) experiments to gather data for a portion of a major research project with an emphasis on gnotobiotic mouse experiments, including fecal sample collection and analysis. Interpret and analyze results, often where few guidelines exist, and make modifications to existing procedures and protocols. Develop new research protocols where appropriate protocols are not described in the literature or where modification or adaptation of standard procedures and protocols is required. Participate in multidisciplinary teams across different faculties or schools. Perform ongoing literature review to remain current with new procedures and related research; apply to ongoing research and development of new protocols. Contribute substantively to the preparation of papers for publication, especially in the results section, and to publication of findings. May present ongoing work to colleagues and/or academic conferences. Oversee supply and equipment budget under supervision of principal investigator or business manager. Work with health and safety department to ensure lab complies with regulations and all required trainings. May supervise (either formally or informally) staff or students as needed, including oversight and direction on techniques, as well as consultation on project work. Serve as a technical resource for other research staff. Oversee the daily activities of the laboratory including lab maintenance; maintain lab stock, manage chemical inventory and safety records, and provide general lab support as needed. May assist with purchasing laboratory equipment.
cond_0065.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in a related scientific field required, with at least two years of demonstrated expertise in a relevant research setting; or Master's degree in a related scientific field.
Proven track record in animal husbandry.
Demonstrated proficiency in mouse handling.
Advanced knowledge of scientific principles.
Strong command of general computer skills with the ability to quickly learn computer programs, databases, and scientific applications.
Exceptional analytical skills and sound judgment.
Ability to maintain detailed and accurate records of experiments and outcomes.
Ability to work under deadlines with general guidance is essential.
Excellent organizational skills and demonstrated ability to accurately complete detailed work.
Minimum 1 year of demonstrated expertise performing mouse husbandry using gnotobiotic isolators, including monitoring mouse conditions and sterilization of materials for introduction into germ-free isolators.
Solid understanding of mouse colony maintenance.
Proficiency in mouse handling and breeding, including oral gavage and blood draw.
Proficiency in basic microbial culture methods.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
Frequently stand, walk, twist, bend, stoop, squat, grasp lightly, use fine manipulation, grasp forcefully, perform desk-based computer tasks, use telephone, write by hand, lift, carry, push and pull objects weighing over 40 pounds. Occasionally sit, kneel, crawl, reach and work above shoulders, sort and file paperwork or parts. Rarely climb, scrub, sweep, mop, chop and mix or operate hand and foot controls. Must have correctable vision to perform duties of the job. Ability to bend, squat, kneel, stand, reach above shoulder level, and move on hard surfaces for up to eight hours. Ability to lift heavy objects weighing up to 50 pounds. Ability to work in a dusty, dirty, and odorous environment. Position may require repetitive motion.
Working Conditions:
May require working in close proximity to blood borne pathogens. May require work in an environment where animals are used for teaching and research. Position may at times require the employee to work with or be in areas where hazardous materials and/or infectious diseases are present. Employee must perform tasks that require the use of personal protective equipment, such as safety glasses and shoes, protective clothing and gloves, and possibly a respirator. May require extended or unusual work hours based on research requirements and business needs.

Interpersonal Skills: Demonstrates the ability to work well with [Company name masked] colleagues and clients and with external organizations. Promote Culture of Safety: Demonstrates commitment to personal responsibility and value for safety; communicates safety concerns; uses and promotes safe behaviors based on training and lessons learned. cond_0222.intro: [Company name masked] Microbiome Therapies Initiative (MITI) is a growing group within [Company name masked], focused on harnessing the microbiome for therapeutic benefit. You will work closely with multiple faculty laboratories from the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences, all focused on human microbiome research. A large part of this role involves staying in regular contact with faculty principal investigators, students, and postdocs across these groups. We are looking for someone with good hands, strong organizational skills, and comfort working with autonomy as part of a collaborative team.
cond_0222.responsibilities:
Independently conduct a portion of the research project(s), with an emphasis on experiments that require use of germ-free mice.
Actively communicate recommendations on experimental design and/or research direction to the multiple faculty principal investigators, students, and postdocs engaged in the microbiome research program.
Independently conduct complex (lab and/or field) experiments to gather data for a portion of a major research project, with an emphasis on gnotobiotic mouse experiments, including fecal sample collection and analysis.
Interpret and analyze results, often where few guidelines exist, and make modifications to existing procedures and protocols.
Develop new research protocols where appropriate protocols are not described in the literature or where modification or adaptation of standard procedures and protocols is required.
Participate actively in multidisciplinary teams across different faculties or schools, contributing to discussions and helping clarify research direction.
Perform ongoing literature review to remain current with new procedures and related research; apply to ongoing research and development of new protocols.
Contribute substantively to the preparation of papers for publication, especially in the results section, and to publication of findings.
Present ongoing work to colleagues and/or academic conferences, walking the audience through methods and findings and handling questions.
Oversee supply and equipment budget under supervision of principal investigator or business manager.
Work with the health and safety department to ensure the lab complies with regulations and all required trainings.
May supervise (either formally or informally) staff or students as needed, including oversight and direction on techniques, as well as consultation on project work.
Serve as a technical resource for other research staff, regularly fielding questions and explaining procedures.
Oversee the daily activities of the laboratory including lab maintenance; maintain lab stock, manage chemical inventory and safety records, and provide general lab support as needed.
May assist with purchasing laboratory equipment.
cond_0222.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in a related scientific field and two years of relevant work experience; or Master's degree in a related scientific field.
At least 1 year of experience performing mouse husbandry using gnotobiotic isolators, including monitoring mouse conditions and sterilization of materials for introduction into germ-free isolators.
Animal husbandry experience.
Comfortable handling mice.
Basic mouse handling and breeding skills, including oral gavage and blood draw.
Ability to work under deadlines with general guidance.
Excellent organizational skills and demonstrated ability to accurately complete detailed work.
Ability to maintain detailed records of experiments and outcomes.
Strong analytical skills and excellent judgment.
Preferred Requirements
Experience with mouse colony maintenance.
Basic microbial culture methods.
Comprehensive understanding of scientific principles.
General computer skills and ability to quickly learn computer programs, databases, and scientific applications.

cond_0228.intro:
The [Company name masked] Microbiome Therapies Initiative (MITI) is a growing group within [Company name masked]. Started in 2019, MITI aims to harness the power of the microbiome for therapeutic benefit and advance human health, a key tenant of [Company name masked]. [Company name masked] is an interdisciplinary institute focused on connecting Chemistry, Engineering, and Medicine for Human Health. The institute was founded as a joint venture of the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences.
The Research Associate, Gnotobiotics will be responsible for overseeing germ-free mouse facilities and facilitating germ-free mouse experiments using gnotobiotic isolators. You will be working closely with multiple faculty laboratories from the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences focusing on human microbiome research, facilitated by [Company name masked] and MITI. Candidates should have good hands and strong organizational skills. Ideal candidates are self-starters, comfortable with autonomy, and embrace opportunities to tackle new problems and challenges as part of a dynamic team in a start-up-like environment within the University.
cond_0228.responsibilities: Independently conduct a portion of the research project(s) with an emphasis on experiments that require use of germ-free mice. Make recommendations on experimental design and/or research direction to the multiple faculty principal investigators, students, and postdocs engaged in the microbiome research program. Independently conduct complex (lab and/or field) experiments to gather data for a portion of a major research project with an emphasis on gnotobiotic mouse experiments, including fecal sample collection and analysis. Interpret and analyze results, often where few guidelines exist, and make modifications to existing procedures and protocols. Develop new research protocols where appropriate protocols are not described in the literature or where modification or adaptation of standard procedures and protocols is required. Participate in multidisciplinary teams across different faculties or schools. Perform ongoing literature review to remain current with new procedures and related research; apply to ongoing research and development of new protocols. Contribute substantively to the preparation of papers for publication, especially in the results section, and to publication of findings. May present ongoing work to colleagues and/or academic conferences. Oversee supply and equipment budget under supervision of principal investigator or business manager. Work with health and safety department to ensure lab complies with regulations and all required trainings. May supervise (either formally or informally) staff or students as needed, including oversight and direction on techniques, as well as consultation on project work. Serve as a technical resource for other research staff. Oversee the daily activities of the laboratory including lab maintenance; maintain lab stock, manage chemical inventory and safety records, and provide general lab support as needed. May assist with purchasing laboratory equipment.
cond_0228.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in a related scientific field and around two years of relevant work experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience; or a Master's degree in a related scientific field.
Some background in animal husbandry.
Comfort handling mice.
Familiarity with scientific principles.
Basic computer skills and willingness to learn computer programs, databases, and scientific applications.
Analytical skills and sound judgment.
Ability to maintain detailed records of experiments and outcomes.
Ability to work under deadlines with general guidance.
Good organizational skills and ability to complete detailed work accurately.
Around 1 year of experience with mouse husbandry using gnotobiotic isolators, including monitoring mouse conditions and sterilization of materials for introduction into germ-free isolators, or equivalent training and hands-on exposure.
Experience with mouse colony maintenance.
Working knowledge of basic mouse handling and breeding skills, including oral gavage and blood draw.
Familiarity with basic microbial culture methods.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
Frequently stand, walk, twist, bend, stoop, squat, grasp lightly, use fine manipulation, grasp forcefully, perform desk-based computer tasks, use telephone, write by hand, lift, carry, push and pull objects weighing over 40 pounds. Occasionally sit, kneel, crawl, reach and work above shoulders, sort and file paperwork or parts. Rarely climb, scrub, sweep, mop, chop and mix or operate hand and foot controls. Must have correctable vision to perform duties of the job. Ability to bend, squat, kneel, stand, reach above shoulder level, and move on hard surfaces for up to eight hours. Ability to lift heavy objects weighing up to 50 pounds. Ability to work in a dusty, dirty, and odorous environment. Position may require repetitive motion.
Working Conditions:
May require working in close proximity to blood borne pathogens. May require work in an environment where animals are used for teaching and research. Position may at times require the employee to work with or be in areas where hazardous materials and/or infectious diseases are present. Employee must perform tasks that require the use of personal protective equipment, such as safety glasses and shoes, protective clothing and gloves, and possibly a respirator. May require extended or unusual work hours based on research requirements and business needs.

cond_0272.intro:
The [Company name masked] Microbiome Therapies Initiative (MITI) is a growing group within [Company name masked]. Started in 2019, MITI aims to harness the power of the microbiome for therapeutic benefit and advance human health, a key tenant of [Company name masked]. [Company name masked] is an interdisciplinary institute focused on connecting Chemistry, Engineering, and Medicine for Human Health. The institute was founded as a joint venture of the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences.
The Research Associate, Gnotobiotics will be responsible for overseeing germ-free mouse facilities and facilitating germ-free mouse experiments using gnotobiotic isolators. You will be working closely with multiple faculty laboratories from the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences focusing on human microbiome research, facilitated by [Company name masked] and MITI. Candidates should have good hands and strong organizational skills. Ideal candidates are self-starters, comfortable with autonomy, and embrace opportunities to tackle new problems and challenges as part of a dynamic team in a start-up-like environment within the University.
cond_0272.responsibilities: Independently conduct a portion of the research project(s) with an emphasis on experiments that require use of germ-free mice. Make recommendations on experimental design and/or research direction to the multiple faculty principal investigators, students, and postdocs engaged in the microbiome research program. Independently conduct complex (lab and/or field) experiments to gather data for a portion of a major research project with an emphasis on gnotobiotic mouse experiments, including fecal sample collection and analysis. Interpret and analyze results, often where few guidelines exist, and make modifications to existing procedures and protocols. Develop new research protocols where appropriate protocols are not described in the literature or where modification or adaptation of standard procedures and protocols is required. Participate in multidisciplinary teams across different faculties or schools. Perform ongoing literature review to remain current with new procedures and related research; apply to ongoing research and development of new protocols. Contribute substantively to the preparation of papers for publication, especially in the results section, and to publication of findings. May present ongoing work to colleagues and/or academic conferences. Oversee supply and equipment budget under supervision of principal investigator or business manager. Work with health and safety department to ensure lab complies with regulations and all required trainings. May supervise (either formally or informally) staff or students as needed, including oversight and direction on techniques, as well as consultation on project work. Serve as a technical resource for other research staff. Oversee the daily activities of the laboratory including lab maintenance; maintain lab stock, manage chemical inventory and safety records, and provide general lab support as needed. May assist with purchasing laboratory equipment.
cond_0272.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in a related scientific field required; advanced degree strongly preferred, with at least 2 years of demonstrated expertise in a relevant research setting; or Master's degree in a related scientific field.
Minimum 1 year of proven, hands-on experience performing mouse husbandry using gnotobiotic isolators, including monitoring mouse conditions and sterilization of materials for introduction into germ-free isolators.
Substantial animal husbandry experience, with demonstrated comfort handling mice.
Advanced knowledge of scientific principles relevant to microbiome or related research.
Exceptional organizational skills and demonstrated ability to accurately complete detailed work.
Strong analytical skills and excellent judgment.
Ability to maintain detailed records of experiments and outcomes.
Ability to work under deadlines with general guidance.
Preferred Requirements
Deep knowledge of mouse colony maintenance practices.
Strong command of basic mouse handling and breeding skills, including oral gavage and blood draw.
Proficiency in basic microbial culture methods.
Expertise in general computer applications, databases, and scientific software, with the ability to quickly learn new platforms.

You will be working closely with multiple faculty laboratories from the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences focusing on human microbiome research. Candidates should have good hands and strong organizational skills. Ideal candidates are self-starters, comfortable with autonomy, and embrace opportunities to tackle new problems and challenges as part of a dynamic team in a start-up-like environment within the University. People who do well in this role often find they can make sense of gnotobiotic methods and microbiome research quite quickly.
cond_0346.responsibilities: Independently conduct a portion of the research project(s) with an emphasis on experiments that require use of germ-free mice. Make recommendations on experimental design and/or research direction to the multiple faculty principal investigators, students, and postdocs engaged in the microbiome research program. Independently conduct complex (lab and/or field) experiments to gather data for a portion of a major research project with an emphasis on gnotobiotic mouse experiments, including fecal sample collection and analysis. Interpret and analyze results, often where few guidelines exist, and make modifications to existing procedures and protocols. Develop new research protocols where appropriate protocols are not described in the literature or where modification or adaptation of standard procedures and protocols is required. Participate in multidisciplinary teams across different faculties or schools. Perform ongoing literature review to remain current with new procedures and related research; apply to ongoing research and development of new protocols. Contribute substantively to the preparation of papers for publication, especially in the results section, and to publication of findings. May present ongoing work to colleagues and/or academic conferences. Oversee supply and equipment budget under supervision of principal investigator or business manager. Work with health and safety department to ensure lab complies with regulations and all required trainings. May supervise (either formally or informally) staff or students as needed, including oversight and direction on techniques, as well as consultation on project work. Serve as a technical resource for other research staff. Oversee the daily activities of the laboratory including lab maintenance; maintain lab stock, manage chemical inventory and safety records, and provide general lab support as needed. May assist with purchasing laboratory equipment.
cond_0346.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in related scientific field and two years of relevant work experience; or Master's degree in a related scientific field.
At least 1 year of experience performing mouse husbandry using gnotobiotic isolators, including monitoring mouse conditions and sterilization of materials for introduction into germ-free isolators.
Animal husbandry experience.
Comfortable handling mice.
Basic mouse handling and breeding skills, including oral gavage and blood draw.
Comprehensive understanding of scientific principles.
Strong analytical skills and excellent judgment.
Ability to maintain detailed records of experiments and outcomes.
Ability to work under deadlines with general guidance.
Excellent organizational skills and demonstrated ability to accurately complete detailed work.
Preferred Requirements
Experience with mouse colony maintenance.
Basic microbial culture methods.
General computer skills and ability to quickly learn computer programs, databases, and scientific applications.

Started in 2019, MITI aims to harness the power of the microbiome for therapeutic benefit and advance human health, a key tenant of [Company name masked]. [Company name masked] is an interdisciplinary institute focused on connecting Chemistry, Engineering, and Medicine for Human Health. The institute was founded as a joint venture of the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences.
The Research Associate, Gnotobiotics will be responsible for overseeing germ-free mouse facilities and facilitating germ-free mouse experiments using gnotobiotic isolators. You will be working closely with multiple faculty laboratories from the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences focusing on human microbiome research, facilitated by [Company name masked] and MITI. Candidates should have good hands and strong organizational skills. Ideal candidates are self-starters, comfortable with autonomy, and embrace opportunities to tackle new problems and challenges as part of a dynamic team in a start-up-like environment within the University.
cond_0488.responsibilities: Independently conduct a portion of the research project(s) with an emphasis on experiments that require use of germ-free mice. Make recommendations on experimental design and/or research direction to the multiple faculty principal investigators, students, and postdocs engaged in the microbiome research program. Independently conduct complex (lab and/or field) experiments to gather data for a portion of a major research project with an emphasis on gnotobiotic mouse experiments, including fecal sample collection and analysis. Interpret and analyze results, often where few guidelines exist, and make modifications to existing procedures and protocols. Develop new research protocols where appropriate protocols are not described in the literature or where modification or adaptation of standard procedures and protocols is required. Participate in multidisciplinary teams across different faculties or schools. Perform ongoing literature review to remain current with new procedures and related research; apply to ongoing research and development of new protocols. Contribute substantively to the preparation of papers for publication, especially in the results section, and to publication of findings. May present ongoing work to colleagues and/or academic conferences. Oversee supply and equipment budget under supervision of principal investigator or business manager. Work with health and safety department to ensure lab complies with regulations and all required trainings. May supervise (either formally or informally) staff or students as needed, including oversight and direction on techniques, as well as consultation on project work. Serve as a technical resource for other research staff. Oversee the daily activities of the laboratory including lab maintenance; maintain lab stock, manage chemical inventory and safety records, and provide general lab support as needed. May assist with purchasing laboratory equipment.
cond_0488.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in a related scientific field required; advanced degree strongly preferred, with at least 2 years of demonstrated expertise in a relevant research setting; or Master's degree in a related scientific field.
Minimum 1 year of proven, hands-on experience performing mouse husbandry using gnotobiotic isolators, including monitoring mouse conditions and sterilization of materials for introduction into germ-free isolators.
Substantial animal husbandry experience, with demonstrated comfort handling mice.
Advanced knowledge of scientific principles relevant to microbiome or related research.
Exceptional organizational skills and demonstrated ability to accurately complete detailed work.
Strong analytical skills and excellent judgment.
Ability to maintain detailed records of experiments and outcomes.
Ability to work under deadlines with general guidance.
Preferred Requirements
Deep knowledge of mouse colony maintenance practices.
Strong command of basic mouse handling and breeding skills, including oral gavage and blood draw.
Proficiency in basic microbial culture methods.
Expertise in general computer applications, databases, and scientific software, with the ability to quickly learn new platforms.

Bachelor's degree in a related scientific field and two years of relevant work experience; or Master's degree in a related scientific field.
At least 1 year of experience performing mouse husbandry using gnotobiotic isolators, including monitoring mouse conditions and sterilization of materials for introduction into germ-free isolators.
Animal husbandry experience and comfort handling mice.
Basic mouse handling and breeding skills, including oral gavage and blood draw.
Experience with mouse colony maintenance.
Ability to maintain detailed records of experiments and outcomes.
Ability to work under deadlines with general guidance.
Excellent organizational skills and demonstrated ability to accurately complete detailed work.
Preferred Requirements
Basic microbial culture methods.
Comprehensive understanding of scientific principles.
Strong analytical skills and good judgment.
General computer skills and ability to learn computer programs, databases, and scientific applications.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS*:
Frequently stand, walk, twist, bend, stoop, squat, grasp lightly, use fine manipulation, grasp forcefully, perform desk-based computer tasks, use telephone, write by hand, lift, carry, push and pull objects weighing over 40 pounds. Occasionally sit, kneel, crawl, reach and work above shoulders, sort and file paperwork or parts. Rarely climb, scrub, sweep, mop, chop and mix or operate hand and foot controls. Must have correctable vision to perform duties of the job. Ability to bend, squat, kneel, stand, reach above shoulder level, and move on hard surfaces for up to eight hours. Ability to lift heavy objects weighing up to 50 pounds. Ability to work in a dusty, dirty, and odorous environment. Position may require repetitive motion.

May require working in close proximity to blood borne pathogens. May require work in an environment where animals are used for teaching and research. cond_0531.intro:
The [Company name masked] Microbiome Therapies Initiative (MITI) is a growing group within [Company name masked]. Started in 2019, MITI aims to harness the power of the microbiome for therapeutic benefit and advance human health, a key tenant of [Company name masked]. [Company name masked] is an interdisciplinary institute focused on connecting Chemistry, Engineering, and Medicine for Human Health, founded as a joint venture of the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences.
The Research Associate, Gnotobiotics will work closely with multiple faculty laboratories from the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences on human microbiome research, supported by [Company name masked] and MITI. In this role, you will help coordinate germ-free mouse facilities and support gnotobiotic mouse experiments alongside faculty, students, and postdocs. Candidates should have good hands and strong organizational skills, and be comfortable working with some autonomy as part of a collaborative team in a start-up-like environment within the University.
cond_0531.responsibilities:
Work alongside faculty principal investigators, students, and postdocs to carry out a portion of the research project(s), with an emphasis on experiments using germ-free mice.
Share input on experimental design and research direction with the multiple faculty principal investigators, students, and postdocs engaged in the microbiome research program.
Coordinate complex lab and/or field experiments to gather data for a portion of a major research project, with an emphasis on gnotobiotic mouse experiments, including fecal sample collection and analysis.
Interpret and analyze results, often where few guidelines exist, and work with the team to modify existing procedures and protocols as needed.
Help develop new research protocols where appropriate protocols are not described in the literature or where modification or adaptation of standard procedures and protocols is required.
Participate in multidisciplinary teams across different faculties or schools.
Perform ongoing literature review to remain current with new procedures and related research; apply findings to ongoing research and development of new protocols.
Contribute substantively to the preparation of papers for publication, especially in the results section, and to publication of findings.
May present ongoing work to colleagues and/or academic conferences.
Help oversee supply and equipment budget in coordination with the principal investigator or business manager.
Work with the health and safety department to help ensure the lab complies with regulations and all required trainings.
May supervise (either formally or informally) staff or students as needed, including guidance on techniques and consultation on project work.
Serve as a technical resource for other research staff.
Support the daily activities of the laboratory including lab maintenance; maintain lab stock, manage chemical inventory and safety records, and provide general lab support as needed.
May assist with purchasing laboratory equipment.

cond_0606.intro:
The [Company name masked] Microbiome Therapies Initiative (MITI) is a growing group within [Company name masked]. Started in 2019, MITI aims to harness the power of the microbiome for therapeutic benefit and advance human health, a key tenant of [Company name masked]. [Company name masked] is an interdisciplinary institute focused on connecting Chemistry, Engineering, and Medicine for Human Health. The institute was founded as a joint venture of the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences.
The Research Associate, Gnotobiotics will be responsible for overseeing germ-free mouse facilities and facilitating germ-free mouse experiments using gnotobiotic isolators. You will be working closely with multiple faculty laboratories from the Schools of Medicine, Engineering, and Humanities and Sciences focusing on human microbiome research, facilitated by [Company name masked] and MITI. Candidates should have good hands and strong organizational skills. Ideal candidates are self-starters, comfortable with autonomy, and embrace opportunities to tackle new problems and challenges as part of a dynamic team in a start-up-like environment within the University.
cond_0606.responsibilities: Independently conduct a portion of the research project(s) with an emphasis on experiments that require use of germ-free mice. Make recommendations on experimental design and/or research direction to the multiple faculty principal investigators, students, and postdocs engaged in the microbiome research program. Independently conduct complex (lab and/or field) experiments to gather data for a portion of a major research project with an emphasis on gnotobiotic mouse experiments, including fecal sample collection and analysis. Interpret and analyze results, often where few guidelines exist, and make modifications to existing procedures and protocols. Develop new research protocols where appropriate protocols are not described in the literature or where modification or adaptation of standard procedures and protocols is required. Participate in multidisciplinary teams across different faculties or schools. Perform ongoing literature review to remain current with new procedures and related research; apply to ongoing research and development of new protocols. Contribute substantively to the preparation of papers for publication, especially in the results section, and to publication of findings. May present ongoing work to colleagues and/or academic conferences. Oversee supply and equipment budget under supervision of principal investigator or business manager. Work with health and safety department to ensure lab complies with regulations and all required trainings. May supervise (either formally or informally) staff or students as needed, including oversight and direction on techniques, as well as consultation on project work. Serve as a technical resource for other research staff. Oversee the daily activities of the laboratory including lab maintenance; maintain lab stock, manage chemical inventory and safety records, and provide general lab support as needed. May assist with purchasing laboratory equipment.
cond_0606.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in a related scientific field and around two years of relevant work experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience; or a Master's degree in a related scientific field.
Some background in animal husbandry.
Comfort handling mice.
Familiarity with scientific principles.
Basic computer skills and willingness to learn computer programs, databases, and scientific applications.
Analytical skills and sound judgment.
Ability to maintain detailed records of experiments and outcomes.
Ability to work under deadlines with general guidance.
Good organizational skills and ability to complete detailed work accurately.
Around 1 year of experience with mouse husbandry using gnotobiotic isolators, including monitoring mouse conditions and sterilization of materials for introduction into germ-free isolators, or equivalent training and hands-on exposure.
Experience with mouse colony maintenance.
Working knowledge of basic mouse handling and breeding skills, including oral gavage and blood draw.
Familiarity with basic microbial culture methods.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
Frequently stand, walk, twist, bend, stoop, squat, grasp lightly, use fine manipulation, grasp forcefully, perform desk-based computer tasks, use telephone, write by hand, lift, carry, push and pull objects weighing over 40 pounds. Occasionally sit, kneel, crawl, reach and work above shoulders, sort and file paperwork or parts. Rarely climb, scrub, sweep, mop, chop and mix or operate hand and foot controls. Must have correctable vision to perform duties of the job. Ability to bend, squat, kneel, stand, reach above shoulder level, and move on hard surfaces for up to eight hours. Ability to lift heavy objects weighing up to 50 pounds. Ability to work in a dusty, dirty, and odorous environment. Position may require repetitive motion.
Working Conditions:
May require working in close proximity to blood borne pathogens. May require work in an environment where animals are used for teaching and research. Position may at times require the employee to work with or be in areas where hazardous materials and/or infectious diseases are present. Employee must perform tasks that require the use of personal protective equipment, such as safety glasses and shoes, protective clothing and gloves, and possibly a respirator. May require extended or unusual work hours based on research requirements and business needs.
Work Standards:
Interpersonal Skills: Demonstrates the ability to work well with [Company name masked] colleagues and clients and with external organizations. Promote Culture of Safety: Demonstrates commitment to personal responsibility and value for safety; communicates safety concerns; uses and promotes safe behaviors based on training and lessons learned. Subject to and expected to comply with all applicable University policies and procedures, including but not limited to the personnel policies and other policies found in the University's Administrative Guide.
